title: MV Need advice with game deployment!

posts.author: Lumpkin
posts.body:
Hey all!
So i'm getting ready to release a demo of my game, however I have many paid assets like images/audio/plugins etc. I'm trying to follow the rules when it comes to keeping these assets encrypted. I know you can encrypt the files when you deploy the game via the RPG Maker MV engine, but I have been told it isn't secure enough?
I need some advice to make my game ready for a demo,  i'm new to this and not sure what the procedure is when it comes to making sure everything is done right. I also need to send out the free game to the asset creators such as Avery/Hiddenone and many more lol.
Any advice is highly appreciated because I don't want to mess up! Thank you.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Lumpkin said:
I have been told it isn't secure enough?
Click to expand...
Who has told you that?
I mean, yes, the truth is that it's pretty easy to crack the default encryption, but there aren't many other viable options out there.
CookTool, as recommended by ShadowDragon, will encrypt everything, but it's a premium product and - well, last time I used it - was dense and difficult to figure out how to use. The cooked game also gets flagged as a false positive by Windows. You can ask
@AceOfAces_Mod
more if you are interested in it. Some of the many patches he has done may have resolved some of those issues.
Regardless, to meet TOS, basic encryption is typically all that is requested unless otherwise specified.
As for contacting them, both are residents of this forum. However, the PM feature has been disabled for users who don't have enough posts (this was to reduce a spamming problem we encountered), so you'd either need to be more active here, or ask them if they have another way of receiving your game.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Lumpkin said:
I know you can encrypt the files when you deploy the game via the RPG Maker MV engine, but I have been told it isn't secure enough
Click to expand...
That is for the seller/original owner to decide.
for all the resources on this websites shop (and their Steam equivalent) the default encryption is enough.
Because theoretically every encryption can be hacked, but if there is an encryption (no matter how weak) then it is legal proof of intent if you get the resources out of there, you can't claim to have accidentally copied them.
Other people might decide that the default encryption is not enough, but then they have to state what kind of encryption they want for their resources in their TOS.
